text:
alice (support): Hey folks, AcmeCorp reporting a sharp p95/p99 spike starting ~14:05 UTC during their billing window. p95 -> 8s, p99 -> 22s, ~3% 503s. They say it feels like scale-up is stalled.

 dave (support): They attached a few traces and timestamps. Customer observed most errors on the Dedicated pool 'ded-acme-usw2'.

 sam (oncall): Looking at infra metrics now. Quick checks: attach-queue length jumped, pool CPU/GPU util ~95%, cold_gpu_init spikes visible.

 lee (eng-sre): Can you paste the sample traces or a small synthetic curl that reproduces? Also need the route id and model variant.

 alice (support): Pasted below. Route: /v1/generate (route_id r-ACME-BILL). Model: gpt-open-8k (quantized). Curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":256}'`

 ci-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042, channel #support. Assigned to @sam. :page_facing_up:

 sam (oncall): Quick dashboard snippets:
```
attach_queue_depth{pool="ded-acme-usw2"} = 118
pool_free_gpus{pool="ded-acme-usw2"} = 1
attach_latency_p95 = 9.8s
cold_gpu_init_time_p99 = 29.3s
provisioning_rate = 0.6 nodes/min (target 2.0)
```

 marta (eng-platform): Provisioner logs show a transient image pull spike in eu-west region during customer billing window; but this is us-west2 customer. Still investigating correlation with scheduler backpressure.

 lee (eng-sre): Two quick possible vectors: 1) Dedicated pool saturated (min_pool too low for burst), 2) Attach fanout / throttles causing backoff. Also auth timeouts can cascade into retries -> thundering attach. Any 401/403 spikes?

 dave (support): No auth errors reported by customer, only timeouts and 503s. However we see a small uptick in auth latency in logs around same time (+200ms).

 erica (sre-lead): Immediate mitigation suggestions — pick one or two and execute: 1) Temp route-level fallback to hosted shared pool for this customer, 2) Increase min_pool for ded-acme-usw2, 3) Enable priority warmup (hot-attach) for the route, 4) Throttle large bulk requests from that API key.

 sam (oncall): I'll do (1) + (3) ASAP. Rolling fallback now: `rictl routing set-fallback --route r-ACME-BILL --target hosted-shared --weight 30`

 sam (oncall): Also enabling hot-attach: `rictl pool update ded-acme-usw2 --hotattach=true --min_pool=2` (will monitor).

 ci-bot: Deploy job queued: deploy/route-fallback-4990001125 by sam.

 lee (eng-sre): While mitigations roll, collect repro steps: 1) Send 200 concurrent small requests in a tight loop to /v1/generate with that key. 2) Watch attach queue and gpu init times. 3) Note any attach handshake errors in logs.

 alice (support): Customer willing to let us test on their key — proceeding with repro now (with their permission).

 sam (oncall): After fallback and hot-attach: attach_queue_depth down to 12, attach_latency_p95 -> 1.1s, p99 down to 3.2s for a few minutes. 503s dropped to <0.2%. Looks effective so far.

 marta (eng-platform): Observed the provisioner backlog: `scheduler.backpressure=true` at 14:03, ramped down ability to launch nodes due to concurrent image pulls across clusters. We're seeing a global image-pull limiter that hit a bad boundary.

 lee (eng-sre): Root candidate: provisioner image-pull rate limiter + low min_pool for this priority customer -> scale-up couldn't keep up, cold GPU init cost high, attach backlog amplified latency. Also auth latency bump made retries pile up.

 erica (sre-lead): Action items (owners):
- lee: dig into scheduler/backpressure metrics and confirm limiter thresholds, correlate with image-pull storms.
- marta: add regional image-pull capacity and increase parallelism for dedicated pools (temp tweak).
- sam: keep fallback in place and monitor customer metrics; coordinate with support comms.
- alice/dave: prepare a short note to AcmeCorp with what we changed and ETA for full fix.

 lee (eng-sre): Quick repro notes from my run: sending 250 concurrent clients saturated attach handshake, I saw attach retries with `handshake_timeout` entries and `attach_throttle` logs. Example log excerpt: 
```
[14:07:12] attach_worker.go:304 attach_throttle: backoff=1200ms id=pool-ded-acme usg=95%
[14:07:14] vm_init.go:88 cold_gpu_init: start id=gpu-03
[14:07:43] vm_init.go:214 cold_gpu_init: ready id=gpu-03 time=29.1s
```

 marta (eng-platform): I'm bumping the image-pull parallelism on the region and will add a temporary exception for dedicated pools serving priority customers. Also increasing default `min_pool` recommendation for customers with high billing-window bursts.

 sam (oncall): After the platform change, provisioning_rate increased to 2.1 nodes/min and attach p99 normalized. I'll keep the fallback in place for 1hr and then step down if stable.

 alice (support): Customer update drafted: short bullet list, what we did, recommend increasing reserved min capacity or scheduling burst outside billing window. Will post once approved.

 dave (support): Customer accepted the workaround and saw immediate improvement. They asked for a postmortem and long-term fix timeline.

 erica (sre-lead): Postmortem owners: lee (root cause analysis) + marta (platform fix + telemetry). We should include: timeline, contributing factors (image-pull limiter, min_pool sizing, attach backoff), mitigation (fallback, hot-attach, image-pull config), and preventative actions (alerts on attach_queue and image-pull throttle, recommend min_pool sizing guidelines).

 lee (eng-sre): I'll start a draft PM/PST and attach the logs & repro steps. Will include a proposed automation: if attach_queue_depth > 50 for a priority route, auto-stage fallback to hosted-shared and page oncall.

 sam (oncall): Leaving fallback rolling at 30% weight and active monitoring. Re-check in 45m.

 ci-bot: INC-2026-042 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring.

 alice (support): Thanks team. I'll keep the channel posted with customer follow-up and PR for postmortem when ready. :thumbsup:
